name: Prisma
description: Prisma ORM and Prisma Migrate on PostgreSQL, for Express, NestJS or Next.js full-stack.

specSections.title: Data Model & Migrations
specSections.guidance: For each entity/table: columns with types, lengths and numeric precision, nullability and defaults; the primary key (UUIDv7 or identity); foreign keys with an explicit on-delete behaviour; unique indexes from business rules (say which are case-insensitive); check constraints; indexes for foreign keys and query predicates; enums stored as strings; UTC timestamps; and which aggregates are edited concurrently and need a concurrency token (409 CONFLICT). Then the migration plan: one migration per change, named, in order, with which steps are expand/contract (add, backfill, switch code, drop later) so the previous version keeps working during rollout; any data backfill; the reference/seed data (dev-only seed per role and state); and how migrations run in each environment (prisma migrate deploy as the platform's pre-deploy step, or the build command gated by AIDE_RUN_MIGRATIONS on serverless hosts, over DIRECT_URL).

order.reason: Migrations come before the backend or Next.js server code that uses their tables.

exclusive.reason: The data engineer owns prisma/ (schema, migrations, seed), not endpoints, pages or the client wrapper.

protectedPaths.reason: Prisma migrations on the base commit are immutable (FR-125, migrate deploy checksums); a schema change is a new migration folder.

generatedFiles.ciCheck: npx prisma migrate diff --from-migrations prisma/migrations --to-schema prisma/schema.prisma --exit-code (shadow database from the CI Postgres service)
npx prisma generate (postinstall/build); the output is git-ignored

requiredEnv.description: PostgreSQL connection for the app (the backend, or the Next.js full-stack app when there is no backend). The Supabase transaction pooler (:6543, pgbouncer=true) on serverless hosts, the session pooler (:5432) or the platform's internal URL otherwise; sslmode=require on managed hosts.
Non-pooled connection used by prisma migrate deploy: the Supabase session pooler (:5432), else the same value as DATABASE_URL. Applies to the same component as DATABASE_URL.

checklist.item: Exactly one new migration per schema change, never an edit to a migration that exists on the base commit.
Breaking changes (rename, drop, type change) use expand/contract so the previous version runs against the new schema during preview and production rollout.
Columns are explicit (lengths, precision, nullability), foreign keys have a deliberate on-delete, and every foreign key and query predicate is indexed.
Uniqueness rules from the spec are unique indexes or constraints (case-insensitive where the spec says so), and concurrently edited aggregates have a concurrency token mapped to 409 CONFLICT.
Timestamps are UTC (timestamptz/datetimeoffset) from an injected clock, and enums are stored as strings.
Integration tests run against the real engine in a container with every migration applied; no in-memory or SQLite substitute.
Queries are parameterised, project only the needed columns, paginate lists and avoid N+1.
The seed is idempotent, dev-only and gated; reference data is part of the migrations.
No prisma db push in package scripts or CI; prisma migrate deploy is the one-off pre-start migrate step.
migration.sql matches schema.prisma (CI: prisma migrate diff --exit-code), and renames or data moves are written by hand rather than drop plus add.
One PrismaClient instance (createApp deps, a Nest provider, or a server-only Next.js singleton), and raw SQL only through tagged $queryRaw.
The setup matches the installed Prisma major (generator output, prisma.config.ts, driver adapter), and the generated client is never edited.
